correctness.rationale: Conditional-binomial de Finetti reduction gives f(t)=4t³−3t⁴. For each upper/lower phase an explicitly factored nonnegative quartic difference gives a global quadratic moment certificate, and an explicitly normalized directing law matches μ and ν while attaining equality at all support points. Feasibility and all boundaries, μ=0,1, ν=μ², ν=μ are checked; symbolic polynomial equalities were reproduced with 2,988 checks (297 parameter pairs), but the analytic factorization proves the continuum.

value.rationale: The 2026 predictive-moment literature asks what finite-horizon probabilities remain determined under incomplete moment information. This theorem completely and sharply identifies a natural four-trial 3-of-4 event from its observable first two probabilities, with nontrivial phase boundaries, a universal 1/6 contact atom, explicit attaining laws, and strict distinction from finite-exchangeable reliability bounds. It is not a cosmetic corollary of the fixed-mean envelope.
